measured: 2026-10-18 on a 2-vCPU VPS (Linux 7.0.0, co-resident live stack); Go 1.27-alpine build CGO_ENABLED=0; redis 7.4.11-alpine3.21 on a dedicated docker network; harness: scripts/benchmark_redis_ratelimit.sh + vegeta v12; each rate a separate 10-20s window with 1-3 repetitions; p95/p99 are per-window end-to-end client-observed latencies
limits_of_this_hardware: 10,000 rps is past the ceiling of this 2-vCPU box even without the limiter (the bare /healthz baseline broke down with multi-second p99s at >=8,000 rps while intermediate runs showed 27-50 ms means - the envelope, not the store, dominates there). The comparisons below are all taken at rates the machine reproduces reliably; the Go microbenchmark numbers carry the per-op cost where thevegeta envelope is saturated.

end_to_end_get_healthz.scenario: sustained GET /healthz (probe class, budget raised to 600000/min for the window), baseline = limiter disabled (API as before the integration), final = limiter armed + Redis token bucket per key

2000rps_15s.base_unavailable: window not repeated at base; see 2000rps_12s cpuA row

8000rps_10s.note: at ~8k rps the envelope itself becomes unstable (two more base windows oscillated between 27 ms and 506 ms mean); base and final are statistically indistinguishable here

end_to_end_auth_rejection.scenario: POST /api/auth/login at 500 rps (auth class default 30/min + 10 burst, all rejected after the burst; 502s are the bench core being absent, not the limiter)

result.note: the rejection path is cheaper than the allow path; early window includes gRPC connection setup

key_cardinality.scenario: 500 distinct X-Forwarded-For identities against the laundered probe class at 2000 rps, 15 s, limiter armed

burst.scenario: 6 parallel vegeta processes x 2000 rps x 6 s (12k target aggregate, actually 11.7k realized)

redis_outage_mid_attack.scenario: POST /api/auth/login at 300 rps for 30 s; store forcible-killed at t=10 s, restarted at t=20 s

result.reading: before the outage the budget rejects (429); DURING the outage the auth class fails CLOSED (503 with Retry-After after the breaker trips) - no traffic silently passes unmeasured; the 503s continue until recovery; afterwards the store answers again (traffic beyond the window shows the allow path restored)
result.recovery: next requests after restart reach the store (validated in follow-up /env-summary and in tests)

go_microbenchmark.note: in-process, one limiter, local redis on the loopback, benchtime 2s; -race clean

pipelined_many_hotkey.note: piggybacking class/report checks on one script call pays for itself

api_process_during_2000rps_12s.note: cgroup cpu.stat deltas; ~8% of one core for the whole HTTP+limiter path at 2000 rps; redis below 1% of a core

redis_connections.note: miniredis false; two instantiations: the API's go-redis pool (5 idle + in-flight) + the bench container's cli

analysis: The token-bucket roundtrip adds ~0.08-0.25 ms p99 end-to-end at every rate the host reproduces reliably (<=4k rps), which matches the ~60-70 us/op in-process Redis cost plus TCP and scheduling. Algo differences at this scale are inside the noise (tb vs sw vs swe within 5 us/op); tb's exact ceiling decides. The store's own share of the host is negligible (memory peak 2.35 MB over all windows with cardinality; cpu sub-1%). The envelope (2 vCPU, GC pauses, vegeta interpolation) dominates above ~4k rps, hence the plan for the 10k case: profile the envelope, not the limiter.
